correctness.rationale: The exact domain is all 8008 labelled six-subsets of the specified sixteen-vertex Cayley graph, over GF(2). The kernel-support induction gives necessity; the canonical P3 and unique isolated-triple extension give a structural 160-fort orbit, and a rank certificate for its representative. Python and C++17 separately evaluate every six-subset and agree on all three disjoint classes 3976,160,3872, including the biconditional. They also verify the explicit basis-exchange obstruction. Code is included for direct replay and does not extrapolate finite outcomes to other graphs.

value.rationale: Six white vertices is the natural common threshold set by the rank-six closed-neighborhood code and known optimal ten-black zero forcing. The new 4032-versus-3872 gap separates linear recoverability from combinatorial one-neighbour peeling and classifies the unique 160-member failure mode as an affine fort orbit. The explicit basis-exchange obstruction shows this discrepancy has matroidal consequences. It is a natural exact finite invariant rather than a chosen arbitrary slice or routine restatement of known forcing counts; broader implications are not asserted.
